# SysPane repository guide for humans and agents

SysPane (System Panel) is a native operational-desktop product family.

Start with `spec/README.md`, `spec/delivery/current-state.md` and the relevant
route in `spec/tools/routes.json`. Read `spec/foundation/authority.md` before
acting. `spec/` owns intended behaviour/contracts; `source/` owns implementation;
`docs/` owns audience-oriented publication. Use `source/`, never a parallel `src/`.

Do not load the entire specification into every subagent. Generate bounded
context with `python spec/tools/specctl.py context --topic TOPIC --out PATH`.
Verify actual repository/ref, dirty state, work scope and execution grant.

Validation from repo root:
```
python spec/tools/specctl.py validate --schemas
python spec/tools/specctl.py generate --check
python -m unittest discover -s spec/tools/tests -v
```
Development-only schema dependencies: `spec/tools/requirements.txt`.
After a reviewed specification change, regenerate and explicitly reseal;
`verify-integrity` checks the sealed delivery bytes, not product correctness.

Preserve the greenfield owned renderer, behind-icon reveal persistence,
wallpaper preservation, native GUI/editor and early cross-platform campaign.
Do not reintroduce Desktop Info or claim a fallback window passes Desktop.
No native/platform test passes are implied by specification validation.

Keep the README a product homepage. Make scoped edits, preserve authored voice,
and place engineering evidence in the proper records. Do not weaken tests,
move published tags, deploy, install services, access signing keys or expand
network/model budgets without corresponding authority. A task admission can
allow routine reversible work without repeated approval prompts.

Before handing off, record changed files, exact refs, actual tests/outcomes,
unexecuted checks, decisions, open questions and the next useful step.
Do not store credentials or private reasoning. Follow `spec/governance/agents.md`.

# SysPane shared repository instructions

Read the root `AGENTS.md` and follow its specification routes.
The canonical project instructions live there and in `spec/governance/agents.md`;
do not maintain a second policy copy in this adapter. Verify the active tool's
instruction-loader behavior rather than assuming all nested files are loaded.

# SysPane — System Panel

A native operational desktop for seeing host identity, network connections,
resources and connected devices at a glance, without replacing your wallpaper.

SysPane is being designed as a native product family with an owned persistent
Windows desktop surface, native Linux and macOS/OS X editions, a diagnostic
inspector and direct desktop editing. Native settings, editor, CLI and automation
share one operation system. Historical targets use explicit capability profiles.

**Current stage: specification and greenfield implementation planning.**
No working native application or supported-platform release is provided yet.

[Read the specification](spec/README.md) · [Current state](spec/delivery/current-state.md)
· [Implementation campaign](spec/delivery/roadmap.md) · [Documentation](docs/README.md)

The project keeps specification in `spec/`, implementation in `source/` and
publication-oriented guides in `docs/`. The specification package includes
local validation, context and non-overwriting bootstrap tools.

License and contribution policy must be selected before public code distribution.
No Microsoft endorsement or upstream acceptance is implied.

# SysPane documentation

This directory owns publication-ready user and developer Markdown, not a second
copy of normative requirements. SysPane is currently at specification stage.

Start with the [product specification](../spec/README.md),
[current state](../spec/delivery/current-state.md), and
[documentation policy](../spec/governance/documentation.md).
The [publication map](../spec/governance/docs-map.json) identifies planned guides
and their source specifications. Create task-oriented pages as real features
become usable; do not publish unimplemented features as shipped functionality.

The optional website/wiki is generated from reviewed repository documents.

name: Specification validation
on:
  push:
  pull_request:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  spec:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      # Immutable v4.2.2 identity checked when this template was prepared.
      # Review/update the pin through dependency maintenance; not a latest-version claim.
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Isolated development dependencies
        run: |
          python3 -m venv .venv
          .venv/bin/python -m pip install -r spec/tools/requirements.txt
      - name: Validate specifications and fixtures
        run: .venv/bin/python spec/tools/specctl.py validate --schemas
      - name: Check generated projections
        run: .venv/bin/python spec/tools/specctl.py generate --check
      - name: Test specification tooling
        run: .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s spec/tools/tests -v
      # Native desktop, privileged lab and signing jobs are deliberately absent.
